paragraphs: Tom and Ben made a board game for the students of their class. The name of the game was Market Run. They drew soup, noodles, and mango on the shopping cards. They ate a snack while they worked. Tom was worried because the rules were long. "Will the students understand them?" he asked. Ben read the rules again and smiled. He sat next to the board and drew the road. "Actually, they are easy," he said.

"How to start. Two to four students can play. Each student gets a piece of a different color. Put your piece on the Gate. Take a shopping card with three foods on it. Throw the dice, and the biggest number goes first.

How to move. Throw the dice, and move your piece. On a green square, you are at a shop. If the shop sells a food on your card, cross it out. On a yellow square, you have a light bag. Move two more squares. On a red square, your bag is heavy. Wait for one turn.
How to win. Cross out all three foods on your card. Then go back to the Gate. The first student at the Gate wins. All the foods in the game are delicious, so have fun!"

On Friday, Teacher Nick came to the table at lunch time. He read the rules and looked at the board. The other students liked the colorful board, too. The board had a gate, a long road, and many small shops. "This is a wonderful game," said Teacher Nick. "Can the class play it at the end of the week?" They played one game at lunch time with two other students. The game took ten minutes, and everyone had fun. Tom was not worried now. Ben put the game in his bag, and it was very light.
